ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure shows a transition-state structure, with HO on the left connected to a carbon skeleton, R1 and R2 labeled on the carbon skeleton, and connected through a dashed line/bond to a nitrogen-containing chain. In the middle, a C–N–N=N–PPh3 fragment can be seen, there is a negative sign near N, and there is a positive sign near the N/P end close to PPh3; there are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: according to the specified method, divide the structure into a non-phenyl transition-state skeleton and a PPh3 part. The non-hydrogen bond connections visible in the non-phenyl skeleton are C–O, C–R1, C–C, C–R2, C–N, N–N, N=N, and N–P, for a total of 8 bond connections. N–P has already been counted among these 8, so when expanding PPh3, only the remaining internal part of PPh3 is additionally counted: P has 1 P–C bond to each of the three phenyl carbons, for a total of 3; the three benzene rings each have 6 C–C bonds, for a total of 18. The additional contribution of PPh3 is 3 + 18 = 21. The total is 8 + 21 = 29.

method.method_draft: Decompose the structure into the non-phenyl transition-state scaffold plus PPh3. Count the visible non-H scaffold links: C–O, C–R1, C–C, C–R2, C–N, N–N, N=N, and N–P = 8 bond links. Then expand PPh3 beyond the N–P bond already counted: three P–phenyl C bonds plus three phenyl rings with six C–C links each, giving 3 + 18 = 21. Add 8 + 21 to obtain 29.

method.method_draft: Assign non-H connectivity degrees from the drawing and abbreviations, then divide by two. For the non-phenyl scaffold and phosphorus center, the endpoint contributions are: O=1, upper carbon=3, lower carbon=3, first N=2, middle N=2, terminal N=2, P=4, R1=1, R2=1, totaling 19 endpoints before phenyl ring internal endpoints. For the three phenyl groups, add 36 endpoints from their internal ring C–C bonds, plus 3 phenyl-side endpoints for the three P–C attachments, giving 39 more. Total endpoints = 19 + 39 = 58, so bonds = 58/2 = 29.
